2) Attached is our vendor onboarding form (filled). On the invoice side we have a couple of quirks: multi-PO invoices, VAT line items, and some suppliers OCR annotate PDFs rather than sending structured CSVs. What are your tolerances for annotated PDFs vs a machine-readable attachment?

Hi Amelia — thanks for sending the form and the context. Short answers up front and then detail below:

- Preferred intake: portal (recommended) for onboarding and ongoing flows.
- Acceptable fallback: vendor email to invoices@redwood.com for initial 60 days, but emails must follow a compact template or include a machine-readable attachment.
- Annotated PDFs: allowed only when the PDF includes a clearly attached CSV or when the PDF text is reliably machine readable and the vendor includes PO numbers in a distinct, parseable field (more below).

Why portal first? predictability and idempotency. Portal gives site-level validation (PO exists, entity mapping) and structured acknowledgement tokens so your AP team can automatically reconcile.

A few implementation details for your ops team and vendors:

1) Compact CSV sample (attached file invoice_template_compact.csv): header row should be exactly: vendor_id,invoice_number,invoice_date,po_number,line_amount,tax,vendor_currency,remit_entity
   - For multi-PO invoices, include one CSV line per PO with the same invoice_number and line-level po_number.
   - If vendors must submit a single PDF combining multiple POs, require an accompanying CSV named <invoice_number>_lines.csv.

2) PO matching rules:
   - Primary match: po_number in CSV line item.
   - Secondary match: subject token "PO:" in email subject or invoice filename if CSV is missing. Example subject: "Invoice INV-12345 PO:PO-9987"

3) PDF annotations and OCR:
   - We will accept annotated PDFs only when the vendor includes an attached CSV or the PDF contains an embedded, machine-readable text layer. Handwritten annotations are not acceptable.
   - For high-volume suppliers that can only produce PDFs, we recommend a short pilot where our ops team verifies OCR quality for 10 sample invoices.

4) VAT and currency: include tax as a separate column in the CSV and a currency code on each line. We do not rely on free-text currency inference.

5) Sandbox & provisioning: if you can share estimated weekly invoice volume and percent multi-PO, we will spin up sandbox access and a scoped rate limit for testing.

I've attached a compact CSV example and a short onboarding checklist we use for enterprise activations.

Attachments: invoice_template_compact.csv (CSV stub), sunnyside_portal_onboarding_checklist.docx (docx stub)

Let me know if you want us to run the OCR pilot or to proceed with portal invites.

Best,

Subject: Re: Vendor activation: invoice routing, PO tie-backs & PDF annotation policy

Thanks Stephanie — this is very helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our side before we confirm volumes:

- For multi-PO invoices: ideally we can avoid vendors splitting invoices into many files. If they send a single invoice PDF with three POs, will Redwood accept one CSV with three lines referencing the same invoice_number? Or do you insist on a separate PDF per PO?

- Remittance: we have two remit entities under Sunnyside (US and UK). We want vendors to put remit_entity in the CSV line. If remit_entity is missing, what's your fallback?

- On annotated PDFs: some of our legacy suppliers add approver initials and a stamp on the PDF. You mentioned handwritten annotations are not acceptable; will a dated initials stamp (machine-printed) be OK?

I'll get back with projected volume by Friday.

Best,
Amelia

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Summary: Sunnyside activation decisions and ops ask (POC + fallback)

Team — quick summary and ops asks so we can queue PROCD-2145: 

Decisions we made with Sunnyside:
- Primary intake: Redwood portal (sandbox to production).
- 60-day email fallback available to invoices@redwood.com for initial go-live. Emails must include either the compact CSV or a CSV embedded alongside the PDF (filename convention required: <invoice_number>_lines.csv).
- Multi-PO handling: accept single PDF + single CSV with multiple lines referencing the same invoice_number. We will not require separate PDFs per PO. This preserves vendor convenience while keeping structured data for matching.
- Remit entity: vendors must populate remit_entity. Fallback rule: if remit_entity is missing we will map by vendor default remit on file; if ambiguous, invoice will go into manual review and vendor will be notified.
- Annotated PDFs: machine-printed stamps/initials OK. Handwritten notes that break OCR are not. Ops to run a 10-invoice OCR quality pilot for legacy suppliers flagged by Sunnyside.

Ops asks (Vanessa / Karthik):
1) Create sandbox organization for Sunnyside and provision 10 test accounts (email invites, API keys).
2) Configure fallback mailbox invoices@redwood.com with a parser that enforces the CSV attachment name convention.
3) Add a validation rule: invoice email subject should include invoice_number or PO token when CSV is missing.
4) Queue OCR pilot and assign to PROCD-2145; link test samples in the ticket.

Related: onboarding form is attached and a Drive link has the sample CSVs and mapping notes.

Attachments: sunnyside_portal_onboarding_checklist.docx
